title: What cannot be done

data.source: Constructor theory (Deutsch 2013; Deutsch and Marletto 2015), as a form of statement. Compared with R6 on 3,000 random protocols, 300 targets and 500 pairs, seeded.

prediction: R6 can be rewritten as a constructor-style law: the task "a half-turn in time T for heat at most Q" is impossible below the line Q T = zeta a squared and possible on and above it, and possible tasks done in a row are possible. Nothing is added by the rewriting.
baseline: The form of law proposed by constructor theory (Deutsch 2013; Deutsch and Marletto 2015): which tasks are possible, which impossible. Decoy: "any time and any heat will do".
why: All five predictions held. Shared: R6 is a possible/impossible statement that composes. Phoenix marks R6 a RESULT that is "existing thermodynamic-length mathematics", conditional on R4, an ASSUMPTION. Left over: constructor theory forbids things in principle and supplies no numbers; R6 supplies a number and holds only for a chosen friction.

forks.path length fixed: the same statement with L for a
forks.friction that varies: zeta_min replaces zeta and the line is no longer reached: a bound, not a dividing line

weighs: All five are mathematics inside R4 and would hold in any world where R4 holds.
result: Of 3000 random ways of making the half-turn, 1719 of them with backward travel, the smallest product of heat and time was 1.0024 times the bound and the middle one 1.416 times. All 300 targets on or above the line were reached. Two possible tasks in a row were always possible (smallest ratio 1.3656); two best halves of unequal length made a whole at 1.125 times its bound. The printed rotor's occasions sat at 1.0148 and 1.0495 times their bounds and its full turn at 1.1547. The seed-coupled rotor made 2000 occasions, all between 1.3613 and 1.8531 long and none outside its bounds.

precise_core: Its principles are stated carefully and some papers are exact; the general theory is still a programme.
proved_by_others: Nearly all of it is by Deutsch, Marletto and close collaborators.
differing_prediction: A proposed witness: if gravity can entangle two masses it is not classical. This is a test design more than a number.
tested: Photon experiments have acted out some of its arguments. The gravity experiment has not been done.
passed: Nothing that differs from standard quantum theory has been tested.
admits_open_problems: Its authors describe it as unfinished and say what is missing.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
